title: How a sequence finds its fold

scenes.visual: Chain morphs through random shapes (3^100 ~ 5e47); log bar chart: random-search time vs age of universe; random search crossed out; energy funnel with ball rolling via intermediates to native state
scenes.narration: Cyrus Levinthal did the arithmetic in nineteen sixty-nine. Even a small protein can adopt an astronomically large number of conformations. Randomly sampling each one, even at the speed of bond rotation, would take far longer than the universe has existed. The only escape from this paradox is that folding does not search randomly. Instead, it follows biased pathways and stabilizes partly correct intermediates, funneling rapidly downhill toward the native state.
scenes.narration_notes_summary: A random conformational search would outlast the universe, so folding cannot be random — it follows biased pathways and stabilizes intermediates, funneling toward the native state.

scenes.visual: Rigid peptide planes joined by two hinges (phi, psi); resonance gauge; sweeping angles fills a phi-psi map; ~15% survives
scenes.narration: Every constraint on protein shape traces back to the peptide bond itself. Because that bond has partial double bond character from resonance, the six atoms around it are locked flat, planarity. That leaves only two backbone bonds free to rotate, phi and psi. But even those are not unrestricted. Steric clashes between neighboring atoms eliminate most combinations. The Ramachandran plot is simply the map of what survives, only about fifteen percent of all phi-psi space.
scenes.slideTitle: From peptide-bond chemistry to allowed conformations
scenes.narration_notes_summary: The logical chain: resonance makes the peptide bond planar, leaving only phi and psi free; steric clashes forbid most of those too; the Ramachandran plot is the ~15% that survives.

scenes.visual: Chain with nonpolar/polar beads in water collapses; caged water released, entropy bar rises; porin inverts the logic in a bilayer
scenes.narration: Water drives folding by pushing non-polar side chains together. Burying them in a hydrophobic core releases ordered water and is entropically favorable. Polar and charged residues sit on the surface of a soluble protein. Membrane porins run the same logic in reverse. Hydrophobic residues face the lipid bilayer, and a polar channel runs through the middle. Folding is at bottom a negotiation between the protein and the chemistry of water.
scenes.slideTitle: The hydrophobic effect is the engine of folding
scenes.narration_notes_summary: Water drives folding: burying nonpolar side chains releases ordered water and is entropically favorable. Membrane porins invert the logic — greasy outside, polar channel within.

scenes.visual: Cloud of candidate conformations filtered by four constraint layers down to one fold
scenes.narration: Start from an astronomical number of possible conformations and four layers of constraint progressively eliminate the wrong folds. Peptide bond planarity removes most options immediately. The preference for trans bonds cuts further. Ramachandran allowed phi-psi combinations constrain the backbone angles. Finally, the hydrophobic effect collapses the chain onto a single stable fold. Constraints are not limitations. They are the mechanism by which a sequence encodes one unique structure.
scenes.slideTitle: Constraints don't limit function — they create it
scenes.narration_notes_summary: The chapter's thesis as a filter: planarity, the trans preference, Ramachandran limits, and the hydrophobic effect each eliminate wrong folds — constraints are how a sequence encodes one unique structure.

scenes.visual: Glu342Lys on a sequence strip; misfolded protein aggregates in liver cell; lacking in blood, elastase eats lung tissue
scenes.narration: Alpha-1 antitrypsin shows how a single amino acid change, glutamate three four two to lysine, causes misfolding with consequences in two separate organs. In the liver, the misfolded protein aggregates inside cells instead of being secreted, damaging the liver. In the lungs, the missing circulating protein leaves the enzyme elastase unchecked, slowly destroying lung tissue and causing emphysema. One mutation, two organ systems: a vivid demonstration of why folding fidelity matters.
scenes.narration_notes_summary: Alpha-1-antitrypsin: one substitution (Glu342→Lys) misfolds the protein, aggregating in the liver and leaving lung elastase unchecked — one mutation, two organs, the cost of a folding failure.
